QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_94

question.text: In a cash-and-carry arbitrage, a trader buys 5,000 shares of a stock at Rs. 250 each and simultaneously sells 5 lots of futures at Rs. 256 (lot size 1,000). Annual financing cost is 8%, applied on a simple 90/365 basis. If the futures expire in 90 days, what is the approximate total arbitrage profit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Step-by-step calculation using a simple 90/365 financing convention: 1. Spot investment = 5,000 x 250 = Rs. 12,50,000 2. Futures value = 5,000 x 256 = Rs. 12,80,000 3. Gross spread = 12,80,000 - 12,50,000 = Rs. 30,000 4. Financing cost = 12,50,000 x 8% x 90/365 ≈ Rs. 24,658 5. Arbitrage profit ≈ 30,000 - 24,658 ≈ Rs. 5,342 The Trap: Rs. 30,000 is the gross spread that ignores financing cost. Rs. 24,658 is just the financing cost. Rs. 0 would only apply if futures were fair-valued. Note: Pages 45 and 94-95 of the Series VIII workbook support deducting financing/carry cost from the cash-and-carry spread to obtain the net arbitrage profit. Workbook compounded or continuous-compounding conventions would produce a slightly different value, so the convention used here is stated explicitly in the stem.
